sources.title: Ujjain District Administration: History
sources.note: Read district history directly. Use Scindia chief town until 1810 and Maratha-period woodworking/paintings only; page contains errors and polemical language in earlier history, not adopted. Grouped with district observatory page.

sources.title: Census of India: Gwalior District Census Handbook (1961), historical introduction
sources.note: Official indexed original confirms Mahadji death in 1794, succession of Daulat Rao and recruitment of Benoit de Boigne. Its 1802 Laswari date is wrong and not used; recapture dates also excluded.

sources.title: William Hunter: Narrative of a Journey from Agra to Oujein (journey 1792), Asiatic Researches VI
sources.note: Complete public-domain OCR downloaded and read. Printed pp. 23 to 25 and 39 to 40. Colonial author describes particular visits, not a representative household survey. Racist judgments, rumored suicide and legendary fort counts omitted. Whole account combined within 200 words.

sources.title: Nandini Chatterjee: Negotiating Mughal Law, chapter 6 (2020)
sources.note: Direct open-access chapter pp. 191 to 210, especially paragraphs about Hindi records and 1787 fārigh-khaṭṭī. All chapters of same book grouped. Dhar outside atlas outline; each example explicitly located. No claim that a seal dated 1783 securely dates the document carrying it.

sources.title: Ujjain District Administration: Observatory
sources.note: Direct official instrument descriptions; Jai Singh origin and later restoration distinguished. Avoid exact foundation year and mistaken ancient astronomy claims on this tourism page.

sources.title: Government of India, PIB: Lokmata Devi Ahilyabai Holkar (31 May 2025)
sources.note: Direct commemorative account. Use Maheshwar court, 1767 permission, public audiences and wells/tanks/rest houses, not inconsistent husband-death chronology, universal prosperity or military superlatives. Maheshwar outside polygon.

sources.title: REHWA Society: Story of Rehwa Society (9 October 2020)
sources.note: Direct interview republished by weaving organization: women taught weaving, Ahilya School for weavers’ children, seasonal designs and shared lunches. Explicitly modern, not evidence of eighteenth-century schooling.

sources.title: Barry Tabor: The Ranas of Gohad and Their Occupations of Gwalior Fort: A Numismatic Perspective, JONS 196 (2008)
sources.note: Direct article pp. 27 to 34. Use figure 5 and conclusion only: rupee 1195 AH/regnal 23 assigned to Gohad occupation in 1781, flower and pistol marks. Historical introductory chronology has mistakes; not relied upon. Whole URL reuse checked against Pandya runtime.

sources.title: British Library Archives: IOR/H/227, Sindhia and Maratha affairs, 1782 to 1783
sources.note: Original indexed catalogue witness recovered by exact shelfmark/URL query; direct page error. Catalogue pp. 1 to 636 describes correspondence 23 May 1782 to 3 July 1783. No claim to have read manuscript letters.

sources.title: National Army Museum: Army of India Medal, Captain John Briggs, accession 1961-03-12-1
sources.note: Original museum catalogue, indexed full description: Second Maratha War 1803 to 1805, Third 1817 to 1818, defeat of Indore at Mahidpur 23 December 1817. Medal authorized 1851, retrospective object not a contemporary campaign issue.

proposedOverrides.name: Mahratta states
proposedOverrides.summary: Northern Maratha states and neighboring communities in the atlas window from 1783 to 1800.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Distinct northern atlas dossier, not an alias upgrade of maratha.
batchIdentityNotes.map: 1783 to 1800; one coarse northern polygon [69.943,22.696,81.301,31.137]. Contains Ujjain, Gwalior, Jhansi, Barua Sagar, Agra and Delhi sample points; excludes Pune, Dhar, Maheshwar, Indore and Shujalpur.
batchIdentityNotes.scope: No claim of uniform rule across included territory. Dhar and Maheshwar examples explicitly neighboring/outside; 1781 coin earlier context; REHWA 2020 later continuity.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: fārigh-khaṭṭī from securely dated 1787 Dhar document in Chatterjee scholarly transcription; Persian prose, mixed-script witnesses. No invented glyphs.
batchIdentityNotes.related: Existing maratha card remains separate; its Britannica source is not used.
